# Neoswarm

> Neoswarm is a terminal workspace for controlling AI agents, built with the extensibility model of Neovim. Every feature is a plugin on a public API, so anything it ships can be replaced by the user. It is free and open source under the MIT license. The command users run is `neosh`.

Key facts:

- The workspace runs as its own process; terminals attach to it as views. Closing a terminal does not stop running agents.
- Plugins are written in TypeScript against `@neosh/api`; the types are generated from the Rust core.
- Every key is a rebindable binding pointed at a named command. Vim-style motions work in lists and in the transcript reader.
- Agents connect through the user's own accounts (Claude, Codex and others). Conversations, files and credentials stay on the user's machine; there is no telemetry.
- Multiple machines can be paired to steer agents remotely, authorized by keys the user approved.

## Pages

- [Home](https://neoswarm.dev/): what Neoswarm is and how it works
- [Plugins](https://neoswarm.dev/plugins/): community plugins, sorted by GitHub stars

## Source and documentation

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/neoswarm/neosh): source code, issues and releases
- [Documentation](https://github.com/neoswarm/neosh/tree/main/docs): guides and architecture decision records
